entry.title: OData V4: Support for Prefer: odata.maxpagesize and $skiptoken Performance in ABAP Environment
entry.content:
Dear SAP Community,

We are currently working to improve the performance of a data retrieval process using OData V4, as it is taking a long time to execute.

Retrieving 10,000 records takes approximately 3 to 4 seconds just for the SAP request-response cycle. We suspect the slowness is caused by high overhead resulting from the fact that only 100 records are retrieved at a time, which necessitates sending a total of 100 HTTP requests using `@odata.nextLink`. Consequently, we are considering ways to increase the number of records retrieved per request.

We would appreciate your insights on the following two points:

1. It is our understanding that in standard OData V4, one can specify the number of records to retrieve at once by setting the `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` HTTP header.
However, when we specified `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` in the ABAP environment for developers, the number of records retrieved per request remained at 100. Is it correct to assume that SAP does not support `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize`? If that is the case, are there any other effective methods for adjusting the number of records retrieved at once?

2. When an OData V4 response includes `@odata.nextLink`, the URL provided contains a value like `$skiptoken=100`, which appears to simply specify an offset.
Since it does not seem to specify a primary key or similar identifier, is it correct to understand that—much like using `$skip`—specifying a value such as `$skiptoken=10000` results in skipping 10,000 records, and that the cost of skipping increases as the value specified in `$skiptoken` grows larger?
If that is the case, it seems that by combining `$top` and `$skip` to retrieve data, one could fetch an arbitrary number of records at once while maintaining performance comparable to using `$skiptoken`. Is this understanding correct?

Thank you in advance for your assistance.

entry.title: User identity not propagated from on-premise Fiori app to BTP service — receiving technical user
entry.content:
We have a UI5 adaptation app running on an on-premise ABAP Fiori Launchpad .
The app calls a CAP service deployed on SAP BTP via an SM59 HTTP destination configured with OAuth 2.0.
The ABAP system correctly identifies the logged-in user .
However, the BTP CAP service receives a technical/service user instead of the real end user.

Current setup
  • UI5 adaptation app served from on-premise ABAP 
  • ABAP system: S/4HANA on-premise
  • SM59 destination to BTP using OAuth 2.0
  • BTP CAP service with XSUAA
What we want
When the logged-in Fiori user triggers an action that calls the BTP CAP service, the CAP service should receive and identify that specific end user — not a generic technical user.

Questions
  1. What is the recommended approach for propagating the end user identity from an on-premise ABAP Fiori app to a BTP CAP service?
  2. Is OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 Bearer Assertion (OA2C_CONFIG with grant type "Current user related") the right mechanism for this?
  3. What needs to be configured on both the ABAP side (SAML2, OA2C_CONFIG, SM59) and the BTP side (XSUAA, Trust Configuration) to make this work end to end?
  4. Does ABAP need to be configured as an Identity Provider (not just Service Provider) in SAML2 for this to work?
Any guidance, blog posts, or step-by-step references would be appreciated.

entry.title: RAP OData V4 unmanaged query pagination
entry.content:
I am implementing a read operation using an Unmanaged Query in the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) for an OData V4 service and pagination.
According to the official SAP Help Documentation page Implementing an Unmanaged Query, the RAP framework handles "default paging" under the following conditions: 

"To avoid high resource consumption when calling an OData service without using $top each OData service, based on the ABAP RESTful Programming Model uses a default paging. This includes... Adding a __next link with a skiptoken to the response if the response represents a partial listing, which is a subset of all available data records." 


However, during runtime testing, when a request is made without a $top parameter, the automated generation of the pagination token does not work as described.
 
Even when configuring the unmanaged query provider class to artificially simulate a partial backend listing—by setting io_response->set_total_number_of_records() to a high integer value (e.g., 1001) while returning a smaller subset array via io_response->set_data() (e.g., 1 row)—the JSON payload returns no __next link or @odata.nextLink tracking property. It only includes the @odata.count attribute.

Questions:
Paging Engine Execution: Why does the unmanaged query engine fail to append a token tracking link when set_total_number_of_records confirms the delivered data payload is a partial listing? 


OData V4 Format Discrepancies: The documentation explicitly references adding a __next link. For a native OData V4 RAP service, the property should structurally be @odata.nextLink. Is this documentation segment incorrect or outdated, or is the framework failing to adapt the token syntax for V4 endpoints? 


Trigger Criteria: What exact internal threshold or API instruction triggers the "default paging" mentioned in the article for unmanaged queries?

entry.content:
I'm getting a consistent 401 Unauthorized calling the API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV sandbox API (A_MatlStkInAcctMod entity), and I've isolated it to something on the sandbox backend, not my credentials.

Request:

 
GET /s4hanacloud/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV/A_MatlStkInAcctMod?$filter=Material eq 'CH_C_104'&$format=json
Header: APIKey: <my key>

Response headers include:

 
www-authenticate: Basic realm="SAP NetWeaver Application Server [EJS/100][alias]"
sap-authenticated: false
sap-system: EJS

This suggests the public API gateway is accepting the request, but the backend NetWeaver system it forwards to is expecting HTTP Basic Auth instead of the API key — a gateway-to-backend mismatch, not an invalid key.

What I've already ruled out:

  • Confirmed the API key is current via "Show API Key" in account settings
  • Regenerated a fresh API key — same result
  • Tested via curl directly and via the API's own "Try Out" tool on this page — same 401 both ways
  • API status on its overview page shows "Active," not deprecated

Timing: the issue started around when the API's page showed "Last Modified: 10 Sep 2026, Version 1.1.0" — possibly related to that update. It's now been several days with no change.

Has anyone else hit this, or is there a known issue with this sandbox after the recent version update? Happy to share my API key ID or further details if useful for troubleshooting.

Update: I tested a sibling entity in the same API product, A_MaterialSerialNumber, and it returns 200 successfully through the same key and the same "Try Out" tool. Only A_MatlStkInAcctMod specifically returns 401. This confirms it's isolated to this one entity's backend, not the API product, key, or subscription as a whole
